facts.text: Francis Ford Coppola, of The Godfather fame, bankrolled this film with $250,000 after being impressed by director Victor Salva's 1986 short Something in the Basement.
Director Victor Salva's 1986 short Something in the Basement won first place in the Sony/AFI Home Video Competition. That win put him on Francis Ford Coppola's radar.
Coppola loaned director Victor Salva the same cameras George Lucas used to shoot American Graffiti (1973).
Coppola's $250,000 is the figure usually quoted for Clownhouse's budget, but TMDB lists it at just $200,000. Either way, it's a tiny budget for a Sundance entry.
This was Sam Rockwell's film debut. He plays eldest brother Randy, and decades later won an Oscar for Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri.
Brian McHugh, who plays middle brother Geoffrey, was only about 14 during filming. Sam Rockwell, playing eldest brother Randy, was 18.
Parts of the film were shot at Francis Ford Coppola's own home in Napa Valley, California.
The film's tagline was "...A circus of the mind."
Clownhouse premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 1989 and was nominated for the Grand Jury Prize in the dramatic category.
Francis Ford Coppola's own 1963 horror debut, Dementia 13, is featured in Clownhouse. The film's executive producer got a nod to his own first movie.
Clownhouse was shot around the same time as Killer Klowns from Outer Space. Director Victor Salva said the two killer-clown productions felt like a race over who copied whom.
Continuity goof: at the clown show, the spotlight lands on Casey's face a moment before the clowns actually aim it at him.
Goof: as Geoffrey leaves the clown tent looking for Casey, the shadow of the camera is visible.
Cinematographer Robin Mortarotti also co-produced Clownhouse with director Victor Salva and Michael Danty. Reviewers single out his shadowy, Halloween-style photography.
The fairground crowd extras were drama students from De Anza High School in Richmond, California, recommended by their teachers when the film shot locally.
Michael Jerome West, who plays the lunatic clown Cheezo, made his feature debut here. He later became a stand-up comedian and appeared on Nash Bridges.
The film is set in fictional Poho County, which director Victor Salva reused in Jeepers Creepers and several of his other films.
A poster on one brother's bedroom door is for Something in the Basement, the 1986 short that got director Victor Salva his Coppola deal.
Clownhouse is full of movie nods. It references The Wizard of Oz (1939), The Wolf Man (1941) and S.E. Hinton adaptation The Outsiders (1983).
Director Victor Salva has a cameo in a yellow shirt in line behind Casey at the carnival ball-toss game. He also voices a radio newscaster.
Body count for Clownhouse: seven. Not bad for a film that reviewers often call a bloodless thriller.
The loud cameras ruined the on-set sound, so the dialogue was re-recorded in post-production. Young star Nathan Forrest Winters spent about a month on it at Coppola's home.
Reviewer Richard Scheib of Moria gave Clownhouse four stars. He called it the only film in the whole slasher cycle to conjure anything like the eerie suspense of Halloween.
Reviewer Kindertrauma praised Clownhouse as a bare-bones thriller that captures the thrill of being left home alone for the first time, even likening it to early John Carpenter.
Continuity goof: the film is set weeks before Halloween, yet the calendar in the mom-and-pop store still shows May.
After Clownhouse, Sam Rockwell moved to New York and trained at the William Esper Studio. He worked as a busboy and a burrito-delivery cyclist before acting paid the bills.
Despite its Sundance debut, the 1990 US theatrical release was brief and mostly in second-run cinemas in places like Iowa, Oklahoma, Vermont and Nebraska.
Variety put Clownhouse on its 2017 list of the creepiest clowns in movies, praising its claustrophobic setting and eerie atmosphere.
British viewers got Clownhouse on VHS in March 1990 from Entertainment in Video, months before its mid-1990 US theatrical run.
TV Guide gave Clownhouse two of four stars, saying it plays cleverly on the visceral dislike many people feel for clowns. Rotten Tomatoes currently shows 33%.
Dread Central put Clownhouse on its Top Six Killer Clown Movies countdown. It called the film a genuinely unsettling tale that delves into the psychology of coulrophobia, the fear of clowns.
Sam Rockwell was 18 when he shot Clownhouse, the summer of 1987, and plays the oldest of the three brothers.
Goof: Casey yanks a lamp from the wall and the socket sparks, even though the power in the house has been cut.
Victor Salva's 2001 film Jeepers Creepers opened Labor Day weekend with $15.8 million, a record for the holiday. Coppola's American Zoetrope financed it.
Salva was convicted of abusing 12-year-old star Nathan Forrest Winters. At Winters' family's request, the film was pulled from home video, and it has been out of print since the 2003 MGM DVD.
After his 1992 release from prison, Clownhouse director Victor Salva worked as a telemarketer while writing scripts. His next theatrical film was Powder (1995).
Shout! Factory turned down releasing Clownhouse through its Scream Factory label because of the controversy around director Victor Salva's conviction.
Years later, Winters picketed a Westwood screening of Salva's 1995 film Powder, which hurt its box office.
The film closes on a title card: "No man can hide from his fears; as they are a part of him, they will always know where he is hiding."
